Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Houston/Galveston TX
558 PM CDT Tue Jul 28 2026

...New AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES...

- A Heat Advisory is in effect for all of Southeast Texas this
  afternoon.

- Hot weather with temperatures in the upper 90s to near 100 and
  heat index values between 105-110 will continue for the rest of
  the week into the weekend.

- Notable rain chances look to return over the weekend.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 110 PM CDT Tue Jul 28 2026

A stagnant ridging pattern has developed and will remain planted 
over the region for the rest of the work week. A surface high
pressure center is observed to our southeast in the Gulf, with a
strong and expansive mid- and upper-level high to our northwest. 
The combination of these two will keep the weather tranquil (for 
the most part) for the next several days. One exception to this is
if we are able to get a seabreeze circulation develop off the Gulf 
and Galveston Bay, it would provide enough low-level convergence 
to trigger an isolated shower or two this afternoon from about 4-8
pm. The chance of a shower developing are generally less than 20%
(with even lower thunder potential), so we did not include any 
mention of this in our forecast at this time.

The main storyline of this forecast is the temperature and heat
index. A Heat Advisory remains in effect for the remainder of 
the afternoon today, but we do not plan to extend the advisory 
into tomorrow at this time. An advisory my ultimately be needed, 
but we are not confident enough at this point to extend/issue a 
new advisory for tomorrow. We realize this is a change from the 
messaging we have been sharing, and a large reason for this is 
that we are seeing signs of deeper/more efficient mixing and
therefore a lower afternoon dew point. This is resulting in heat
index values a little lower than the medium-range guidance was 
indicating, even as recently as yesterday. As a result, our heat 
index forecast for the next few days is expected to peak around 
105-108. Our Heat Advisory criteria is a heat index of 108, so our
forecast is currently sitting within a degree of advisory criteria 
for a few hours Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday afternoon. Each 
day we will likely hold off to issue an advisory until we get a 
better read on that day's diurnal trend. A trade-off of the deeper 
mixing will be higher ambient temperatures, particularly Thursday, 
Friday, and Saturday as the ridge to our northwest flattens and 
sends increased subsidence our way. This opens the door for
100-degree days for at least parts of the region each of those 
afternoons. How likely depends on the exact location, but by-in- 
large, the chance of the high temp reaching 100 is around 20-30% 
today and tomorrow, 40% on Thursday and Friday, closer to 50% on 
Saturday, then back down to 20-30% Sunday onward.

It's worth noting that we're still forecasting heat index values
between 105-108 each afternoon. At the end of the day, the human
body and animal's response to heat does not vary much between 107
and 108...therefore proper heat safety messaging and precautions 
should continue to be taken regardless of the presence of an 
advisory or not.

We briefly alluded to the ridge flattening and lower 100-degree 
probabilities late in the weekend into early next week. An upper 
trough is forecast to develop over the Eastern CONUS late this 
weekend into early next week, with a backdoor "cold" front
forecast to inch closer to our forecast area. It's too soon to
know exactly how far southwest the front will get, but either way, 
slightly increased PoPs (20-30%) and more seasonal temperatures 
are forecast next week.

&&

.AVIATION...
(00Z TAF Issuance)
Issued at 538 PM CDT Tue Jul 28 2026

Winds decrease this evening, shifting southwesterly overnight into
early Wednesday. Low decks around 1500-2000ft develop during this
early morning period, could see some isolated MVFR CIGs/patchy
fog, though otherwise brief in nature. Winds increase and shift
southeasterly during the daytime on Wednesday with VFR conditions
prevailing.

03

.MARINE...
Issued at 110 PM CDT Tue Jul 28 2026

Light to moderate onshore flow and 2 to 4 foot seas will continue
for most of the week. With surface and upper-level high pressure 
dominating, rain chances will be minimal through the work week.
Southwesterly winds increase and seas build somewhat over the
weekend, which may prompt the issuance of caution flags.

Bonnette

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Lake Charles LA
1117 PM CDT Tue Jul 28 2026

...New DISCUSSION, MARINE, FIRE WEATHER...

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Dangerous heat continues with temperatures in the upper 90s to 
  100s and heat indices of 105-110F.

- A Heat Advisory is in effect for Areas east of I-49 and along
  the Atchafalaya.

- Rain chances and slightly cooler temperatures arrive late in the
  work week and into the weekend. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
(Tonight through next Tuesday)
Issued at 1044 PM CDT Tue Jul 28 2026

Bulk of forecast considerations tonight were taken in by heat
indices tomorrow (Wednesday.) The persistence forecast will
prevail until tomorrow with the start of a pattern change taking
place sometime Thursday. High pressure regime remains in place,
and in fact, may be enhanced some on Wednesday. Upper low pressure
and trof descend from the northeast US, which lays the framework
for later waves to erode upper high pressure. In the meantime, it
appears the trof only acts to compress high pressure over the
central US, and ultimately increase heights on Wednesday. While
this will likely result in slightly higher temps Wed, it will also
mean mixing once again. Since the airmass overtop the region mixed
out quickly before those advisory-criteria indices really set in,
it meant that most of the region stayed at and under 108 today.
Since the same scenario may play out Wed, the bulk of the area 
was left out of an advisory. Those in Alexandria and along the 
Atchafalaya may hit 108 to 110, even with mixing, so those areas 
did get an advisory for the day. 

There is the part of the seabreeze pushing in during the early
afternoon which may poke heat indices up a skosh, but if it was 
like today, even that moisture plume could be mixed down quickly. 
Unless there is a notable change in presentation or forecast 
overnight, the advisory will stand as-is. But adjustments may come
as deemed necessary. 

High pressure will try to hang on into Thursday which may bring
about this conversation again, but considering the increase in
moisture that's anticipated with the approaching east trof, there
could be enough cloud cover to tamp temps down from the needed
highs to bring about advisory criteria Thursday to the end of the
week. 

Residual high will also deflect majority of rain chances to the
east until it can back off sometime later Thursday or Friday. 

11/Calhoun

&&

.MARINE...
Issued at 1044 PM CDT Tue Jul 28 2026

Low seas and moderate onshore winds will prevail to the end of the
work week as high pressure largely remains in charge. High
pressure will begin backing into central Texas late Thursday into
Friday, igniting a pressure gradient and increasing easterly
winds. This may result in a period of Small Craft Advisory
conditions and very likely will signal the return of some rain
chances over coastal waters. 

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 1044 PM CDT Tue Jul 28 2026

High pressure will hang on into Wednesday and likely into much of
Thursday, continuing the anomalously hot and dry pattern these
days. Daytime RH minimums will vary in the 45 to 60 percent range
through the end of the week, increasing into the weekend with the
return of rain chances.
